transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Gupta (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Cobalt CTO), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Jorge Mendes (SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick checkin; hope the calendar time still works for you. we'll run through latest numbers vs your baseline provider and then call out experiments.
[00:18] Liam: Yep this time's good, thanks. Priya's on mute but she's here.
[00:25] Maya: All right, I pulled the latest runs from last night, there's a mixed set of workloads — 512 token prompts, 2k and 4k conversational sequences. I also uploaded the raw logs to the sheet, link in chat.
[00:40] Priya: Saw that, thanks. Quick note: our baseline provider numbers are from last month, their endpoint uses 8xA100 with some custom batching.
[00:50] Samir: Good context. high-level summary: on the 512 token QA workload we beat baseline p50 by ~12ms and p95 by ~60ms; on 2k sequences we're comparable at p50 and slightly worse at p95, and on 4k the baseline edges us on throughput due to bigger efficient batching on their infra.
[01:12] Jorge: When you say "edges us" do you mean peak QPS or sustained? we care about sustained under our typical traffic.
[01:19] Maya: For 4k it's peak throughput — baseline shows higher sustained QPS under large batch sizes. But there's nuance: their pipeline drops accuracy a bit when they quantize aggressively.
[01:33] Priya: Right, accuracy tradeoff is a factor. we can't bring quality down too much. what's the delta on quality you saw?
[01:39] Maya: On our eval prompts, the baseline's heavy quantization caused slightly noisier completions in ~6% of cases, mostly formatting/structured output drift. Our quantized configs keep that under 2%.
[01:52] Samir: So we have a cost/latency tradeoff vs quality; we emphasized earlier that we can tune quantization profiles and kernel selection per-model to get closer on throughput without losing quality.
[02:06] Liam: For production we need p95 under 850ms and sustained throughput around 120 QPS for the nightly batch jobs, plus spikes to 400 QPS for user-facing. can you map current numbers to those targets?
[02:19] Maya: Sure. For the 2k conversational test our p95 is ~720ms when running on the dedicated test pool with continuous batching configured. For 4k it's ~1.1s p95 at current config at 100 QPS. So 4k currently misses the 850ms p95 target.
[02:37] Samir: That's why the next experiment is key — enabling more aggressive prefix KV-cache and adjusting batch windows. We think we can bring 4k p95 down to ~800–900ms without quality regression.
[02:50] Priya: When you say prefix KV-cache, do you mean caching previous context on the same session to avoid recomputation?
[02:55] Maya: Exactly. For conversational flows where prior tokens recur, caching KV reduces expensive re-attention for earlier tokens. Also smarter batching based on seq-len distribution helps.
[03:05] Jorge: Any changes needed on our side? network, headers, tokens?
[03:09] Samir: No infra changes. it's config on the Redwood side, and we might need a short rollout window to test canary. we'll keep traffic routing to baseline for the spikes until we validate.
[03:19] Liam: Ok. show of hands, are we comfortable running a canary test for the KV-cache + batching on the 4k workload?
[03:25] Priya: Yes, assuming we can see p95 and tail latencies live and we can instantly roll back.
[03:30] Maya: We'll set an automatic fallback if tail latencies exceed thresholds, yes.
[03:34] Samir: Great. I want to call out one anomaly in last night's logs: a few 99th percentile requests spiked much higher than normal — looking like garbage collection pauses on one instance. we've flagged it and will share raw logs.
[03:47] Jorge: That aligns with some intermittent CPU steal we saw on our side around 02:00 UTC. we'll correlate our infra logs.
[03:53] Priya: On cost, how do we compare with baseline for the 2k and 4k runs? they claim lower unit cost at scale.
[03:59] Maya: When you factor in quality-adjusted cost (i.e., cost per successful/accurate response), Redwood is comparable for 2k and slightly higher for 4k in current configs. But with KV-cache and better batching we project 20–30% cost reduction on 4k.
[04:14] Samir: Also remember routing policy — for cheaper, non-sensitive background workloads you can route to baseline; for user-sensitive live traffic route to Redwood. hybrids are common.
[04:25] Liam: Yep that's our current plan if you can guarantee the fallback.
[04:29] Maya: We'll set up automated routing + canary with rollback rules. I'll attach the canary runbook.
[04:36] Samir: Quick note on security questions that popped up from procurement: they asked for SOC 2 type II report, SAML SSO flows, and KMS integration details. We have those docs; I'll resend them after the call.
[04:50] Priya: Good. also need audit log retention config — we need 1 year for compliance.
[04:55] Samir: We support configurable retention; I think the default is 90 days but enterprise tiers can do 1 year. I'll confirm and add to the sheet.
[05:04] Liam: Back to benchmarks — can you walk through the spreadsheet briefly? i opened it.
[05:09] Maya: Sure. (screen shares) first tab is p50/p95/p99 for each model and sequence length. second tab is throughput graphs with QPS vs latency, third tab is raw request logs compressed. Notice the vertical lines where we toggled batching configs.
[05:25] Priya: I see a big bump at 02:12 in the 4k run. is that the same GC anomaly?
[05:30] Maya: likely yeah. We'll annotate those rows.
[05:33] Jorge: For the canary, can we limit to a small % of sessions and only for non-critical users?
[05:38] Samir: Absolutely, we can do 1% to start and ramp to 10% if metrics look good.
[05:42] Priya: one more: do you have a recommended quantization profile for our models to balance latency with quality?
[05:48] Maya: We recommend per-model profiles; for your 2k-heavy models q4_0 gives most latency wins with minimal quality loss; for 4k conversational q4_K_S* (placeholder name) with selective layers kept in fp16 works best. We'll include explicit config in the spreadsheet.
[06:05] Liam: timeline — if we start canary next week how long until we see meaningful numbers?
[06:11] Samir: With 1% traffic we get tail metrics in 24–48 hours; I'd recommend a 72 hour canary window to be safe.
[06:17] Priya: ok that works. We'll confirm internal stakeholders and prod QPS patterns by Monday.
[06:22] Samir: Next steps recap: I'll share updated benchmark sheet + raw logs; Maya runs KV-cache + batching on 4k and posts results; Priya provides QPS pattern. We'll sync next Thursday same time.
[06:34] Liam: Sounds good. thanks all.
[06:36] Samir: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up in email with the sheet and the SOC docs.
[06:40] (call ends)

Notes: transcription has occasional recognition errors (proper nouns, acronyms). Links shared during call: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/Cobalt-4k (benchmark spreadsheet), runbook link: https://redwood.app/runbooks/canary-kv-cache
